name: E-ZPass New York and Tolls By Mail NY
notes: Researched from public NYS Thruway Authority pages (About E-ZPass, About Tolls by Mail, What is Cashless Tolling, Toll Payer Advocate). e-zpassny.com itself sits behind a bot check that was not bypassed, so its sign-in wording, statement options and fee pages were not read; those keep the family defaults. E-ZPass NY is a prepaid account (tolls debited directly), up to four tags per account; On-the-Go tags cost $25 at retailers. Tolls by Mail bills arrive 30-45 days after travel; an unpaid bill brings a second bill with a $5 late fee, then a violation with a $50 fee per notice (Thruway), then collections (Transworld Systems); three or more unanswered violations in five years can suspend a registration. Pay Tolls by Mail online, in the Tolls NY app, by automated phone (1-800-333-8655), by mail, or with cash at retailers using the bill's barcode. The Toll Payer Advocate helps with unresolved Thruway issues but not with DMV suspensions. No installment plan is described on the pages read. Reviewer (2026-10-09): e-zpassny.com still returns no readable content; Thruway pages re-read and confirm up to four tags, the $25 On-the-Go tag, up to 75% savings, bills 30-45 days after travel, $5 second-bill late fee, $50 per violation notice, TSI collections after 30 days, the three-violations-in-five-years suspension rule, all five Tolls by Mail payment channels and the Toll Payer Advocate limits. thruway.ny.gov is the operator's domain and acceptable as official. Reviewer (2026-10-09, run 2): the catalog's synthetic 3/6/12-month online payment plan was removed (payment_arrangement unsupported, evidence inferred): no official page read, nor a web search, describes an installment plan for this agency, so the mock now points to customer service instead.

guest_pay.note: Tolls by Mail bills are paid online, in the Tolls NY app, by phone, by mail or with cash at retailers.

payment_assistance.note: The Thruway Toll Payer Advocate helps customers who could not resolve a Thruway toll issue with the service center.

payment_arrangement.note: No installment plan is offered online. Pay Tolls by Mail bills in full by the due date; call the E-ZPass NY Service Center about a balance you cannot pay, or the Toll Payer Advocate if it stays unresolved.

help.title: About E-ZPass NY
paragraphs: E-ZPass is a prepaid account: tolls are debited from it automatically, often at a discount of up to 75% off the Tolls by Mail rate in New York. One account can have up to four tags.
Keep your address, license plates and payment information current so you do not get toll bills. Manage the account online or in the Tolls NY app and turn on alerts.
Open an account online, by mail, in the Tolls NY app, or buy a $25 On-the-Go tag at a participating retailer and register it online or by phone.

help.title: Paying a Tolls by Mail bill
paragraphs: Without E-ZPass, cameras capture your plate and a Toll Bill is mailed to the registered owner 30 to 45 days after the trip; you can sign up for a text when tolls are ready to pay.

Pay online, in the Tolls NY app, with the automated phone system at 1-800-333-8655, by mailing the coupon and a check (no cash) to the Tolls by Mail Payment Processing Center, PO Box 15183, Albany, NY 12212-5183, or with cash at a local retailer using the bill's payment barcode.

help.title: Late fees and violations
paragraphs: Pay the Toll Bill by its due date. If it is late, a second Toll Bill adds a $5 late fee. An unpaid second bill becomes a violation with a $50 fee per violation notice on Thruway tolls; other New York authorities set their own fees.
Violations unpaid after 30 days can go to a collection agency. Ignoring three or more Notices of Violation within five years can lead to suspension of the vehicle's registration by the DMV.

help.title: Toll Payer Advocate
paragraphs: If you could not resolve a Thruway toll or violation with the E-ZPass NY Service Center, the Thruway's Toll Payer Advocate can review it. Have the plate, account number, violation number and a record of your attempts ready.
The advocate handles Thruway travel only and cannot help when a registration is pending suspension or suspended for unpaid Thruway tolls.
